Exempt vs non-exempt:
who gets overtime

lines.text: Paid under $684 a week? You're usually owed overtime.
lines.say: Paid under six eighty-four a week? You're usually owed overtime.

lines.text: That's the federal salary floor for most exempt white-collar jobs, which also need exempt duties: $35,568 a year.
lines.say: That's the federal salary floor for most exempt white-collar jobs, which also need exempt duties: thirty-five thousand five hundred sixty-eight dollars a year.

lines.text: Non-exempt workers get time-and-a-half after 40 hours a week. Exempt workers don't.
lines.say: Non-exempt workers get time-and-a-half after forty hours a week. Exempt workers don't.

lines.text: Hypothetical: $20 an hour for 50 hours. With overtime that's $1,100, versus $1,000 at straight time.
lines.say: Say twenty dollars an hour for fifty hours. With overtime that's eleven hundred dollars, versus a thousand at straight time.

lines.text: The floor has moved: $455 in 2004, $684 in 2020. A 2024 rule to raise it was struck down that November and rescinded in May 2026.

lines.text: From 2025 through 2028, eligible workers can deduct that overtime premium from federal income tax, up to $12,500, or $25,000 filing jointly.
lines.say: From twenty twenty-five through twenty twenty-eight, eligible workers can deduct that overtime premium from federal income tax, up to twelve thousand five hundred, or twenty-five thousand filing jointly.

lines.text: Only the extra half of time-and-a-half counts: in that example, $100 of the $1,100.

post.title: Under $684 a week? The overtime rule, explained
post.ig:
Paid under $684 a week? You're usually owed overtime past 40 hours.

Most exempt white-collar jobs need a salary of at least $684/week ($35,568/yr) plus exempt duties; non-exempt workers get 1.5x after 40 hours.
Hypothetical: $20/hr for 50 hours = $1,100 with overtime vs $1,000 straight.
The 2024 rule raising the floor was vacated in Nov 2024 and rescinded by DOL in May 2026. For 2025-2028, eligible workers can deduct the overtime premium from federal income tax (income limits apply), up to $12,500 ($25,000 joint).
Some jobs, like teachers, doctors, lawyers and outside sales, have no salary test, and some states set higher floors.

Sources: U.S. Department of Labor; IRS.

Most exempt white-collar jobs require a salary of at least $684 a week ($35,568 a year) plus exempt duties; non-exempt workers get time-and-a-half after 40 hours. The 2024 rule that would have raised the threshold was vacated in November 2024 and rescinded by the Labor Department in May 2026. For 2025-2028, eligible workers can deduct the overtime premium from federal income tax (income limits apply), up to $12,500 ($25,000 joint). Some jobs, like teachers, doctors, lawyers and outside sales, have no salary test, and some states set higher floors. Sources: U.S. Department of Labor, IRS.
